get-spec output:
Current public/llms.txt is stale: it lists hidden/removed games (connections, heatmap, stat grids) and wrongly calls the app a single-page React application (it is Next.js SSR/App Router). Research findings (llms.txt v2 spec, llmstxt.org, Aug 2026): required structure is one H1 site name, a one-paragraph blockquote summary, optional plain paragraphs, then ## sections each a Markdown link list (Title, url, one-line note). Content rules: 10-30 curated links grouped by product surface not site hierarchy, absolute https URLs, a Last reviewed date line, no marketing fluff, no tech-stack trivia, no auth-gated or hidden-feature links. Honest caveat backed by traffic data (Google explicitly says it is not used for Search; measured AI-agent logs show well under 1 percent of sites get any llms.txt fetches at all): treat this as cheap hygiene, not an SEO lever, but a stale file that misinforms agents is worse than none. Task: rewrite public/llms.txt to list exactly the current visibleGames from src/utils/GameUtils.tsx (10 games today, do not hardcode a count that will drift), remove every hidden game and the /admin mention, add a short accounts/leaderboard/multiplayer section, and a Last reviewed date. Keep it under about 40 lines. Bonus if time allows: add app/llms.txt/route.ts generated from visibleGames so this cannot go stale again, and a small <link rel=describedby href=/llms.txt type=text/markdown> tag in the root layout per the v2 discovery convention.
